title: The Recall Charter
description: A citizen-led effort to draft a model Right to Recall framework that state assemblies can adopt. Transparent, constitutional, and built in the open.
objective: Produce a model Right to Recall bill that any state assembly can introduce without redrafting from scratch, complete with constitutional safeguards, signature thresholds, and timelines.
background:
India has no uniform recall law. Provisions exist in municipal and panchayat statutes across several states, but they vary widely in threshold, procedure, and enforceability. Legislators sympathetic to reform have repeatedly cited the absence of a credible draft as a reason for inaction.

The Charter closes that gap. It is written in the open by constitutional lawyers, political scientists, and citizens, with every revision published for public comment.
why: A demand without a draft is a slogan. Handing legislators a ready, rigorously reviewed bill turns an argument into something that can actually be tabled, debated, and voted on.
milestones:
DONE | 2025-03 | Drafting committee convened with 14 contributors
DONE | 2025-06 | Public comment round one closed, 2,400 submissions reviewed
DONE | 2025-09 | Constitutional review completed by independent counsel
ACTIVE | 2025-12 | Gathering 100,000 citizen endorsements
NEXT | 2026-03 | Formal submission to first state assembly

title: Campus Democracy Drive
description: Bringing civic literacy workshops to 500 colleges. Teaching first-time voters how accountability tools like recall actually work.
objective: Run a two-hour civic accountability workshop in 500 colleges, reaching first-time voters before their first general election.
background:
More than half of India is under 30, and most first-time voters have never been taught how to hold a representative to account between elections. Civics education stops at how a bill becomes law.

The Drive supplies a ready-to-run workshop kit -- slides, a facilitator script, and a mock recall exercise -- so any student body can run a session without prior training.
why: Habits of participation form early. A voter who has traced a representative's record once is far more likely to keep doing it for the next forty years.
milestones:
DONE | 2025-02 | Workshop curriculum piloted at 12 colleges
DONE | 2025-05 | Facilitator kit translated into 6 languages
ACTIVE | 2025-11 | 180 of 500 colleges reached
NEXT | 2026-02 | Student facilitator training programme launches

title: Transparency RTI Push
description: Equipping citizens with ready-to-file RTI templates to track representative performance and public spending in their constituency.
objective: Publish a free library of pre-filled RTI templates covering attendance, constituency development fund spending, questions asked in the house, and project completion.
background:
The Right to Information Act is one of the most powerful accountability tools available to an Indian citizen, and one of the least used. The barrier is rarely willingness -- it is not knowing how to phrase a request so it cannot be dismissed on a technicality.

Each template in the library has been filed at least once and refined based on the response actually received.
why: Recall only works if citizens have evidence. RTI is how that evidence gets gathered, and a template turns a two-hour research task into a five-minute one.
milestones:
DONE | 2025-08 | First 12 templates drafted and test-filed
ACTIVE | 2025-12 | Legal review of template wording
NEXT | 2026-01 | Public library launch with filing tracker
NEXT | 2026-04 | Response database opened for public search

title: Local Body Accountability
description: A pilot in municipal wards where recall provisions already exist, documenting how communities use them responsibly.
objective: Document how recall provisions already on the books in municipal and panchayat law are used in practice, and publish the findings as evidence for state-level reform.
background:
Recall is often dismissed as untested in India. It is not. Several states permit recall of municipal and panchayat representatives, and those provisions have been exercised.

This pilot followed wards across four states, recording how petitions were initiated, what safeguards prevented misuse, and what turnout thresholds actually looked like in practice.
why: The strongest answer to "recall will be abused" is a record of it not being abused. This study produced that record.
milestones:
DONE | 2024-10 | Field study designed with 4 partner organisations
DONE | 2025-01 | 38 wards surveyed across 4 states
DONE | 2025-05 | Findings peer-reviewed
DONE | 2025-07 | Report published and submitted to two state commissions
